topSignals.title: PJM files "Bring Your Own New Generation" (BYONG) tariff with FERC, formalizing the self-supply advantage for behind-the-meter SOFC
topSignals.text: PJM's Board filed with FERC on August 13 (targeting an October 12, 2026 effective date) a package built around a new Large Load Registry tracking every 50 MW+ site and whether it brings its own generation. Loads that don't self-supply face first-in-line curtailment starting June 1, 2027, compensated at only 50% of PJM's existing demand-response penalty rate. Loads that do self-supply, e.g. via on-site SOFC, qualify for an expedited "BYONG" interconnection track targeted to go live this month. This is the first concrete, tariff-backed mechanism replacing the vague "BYOG expedited track" this digest has tracked as a placeholder since August 17, and gives the LCOE model an actual curtailment-risk premium to price behind-the-meter SOFC against. RTO Insider | PJM Inside Lines | Forbes | Tom's Hardware

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy now down roughly 49% from its August 12 record close, with no single new negative catalyst
topSignals.text: BE has slid from $391 (the August 12 record) to roughly $200 as of August 21-22, including a 13.5% drop in the week that saw the August 19 Power Connect launch, itself a positive product announcement. Q2 2026 results were record-strong (revenue $1.065B, +166% YoY; FY2026 guidance raised to $3.9-4.2B) and are not the driver. The move reads as a valuation reset from ~81x forward earnings compounding the unresolved scandium-sourcing overhang, not a new operational problem. Market cap is now roughly $60B, down from ~$70B a week earlier. Motley Fool | Yahoo Finance

topSignals.title: EIA cuts 2026 Henry Hub forecast again, to $3.44/MMBtu
topSignals.text: The August Short-Term Energy Outlook lowers the 2026 average more than 6% from July's $3.67/MMBtu, with Q3 2026 averaging $2.87/MMBtu, the lowest quarterly figure of the year. This confirms the low-gas environment already flagged from spot data ($2.68-2.80/MMBtu) in the August 21 digest and further widens the gap versus the $4.00-4.90/MMBtu figure still used as this model's background gas-price case. EIA STEO | Rigzone

Other players: Quiet day. No new dated announcements from Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, or Sunfire beyond items already logged in prior digests.

Project Jupiter (Oracle/OpenAI, NM, 2.45 GW Bloom SOFC): Both NM Supreme Court emergency petitions (New Energy Economy's air-permit stay, filed August 19; Center for Biological Diversity's water-well challenge, filed August 20) remain undecided as of August 22. No ruling found in today's search; the September 14 NMED hearing status is still contingent on the Court's response. ABQ Journal
Other pipeline items (Crusoe/Cheyenne, Hedgehog Texas, Nebius/Bloom NJ, Equinix, FCEL/Fit Energy, PowerCell/ECL Santa Clara): no updates today; status unchanged from August 21.

PJM BYONG/Large Load Registry filing (see Top Signal #1): Filed August 13, requested effective date October 12, 2026. Part of a broader PJM Board package (July 27 decisional letter) that also renames "Connect and Manage" to "Interim Resource Adequacy Service" and adds a Reliability Backstop Procurement auction starting September 2026. Appears to supersede or incorporate the narrower May 18 co-location filing (ER26-1088-001) tracked since August 17-18. RTO Insider | White & Case

Background unchanged: FERC RM26-4 comment period open through ~September 16; ERCOT Batch Zero audit (250-300 projects) targeted for completion by December 2026; ITC 48E 30% credit active for all fuel cell feedstocks; Germany EnEfG PUE/ERF/waste-heat rules from July 2026.

Bloom Energy (BE): See Top Signal #2 for the price move and drivers. Scandium class-action lead-plaintiff deadline remains September 28, 2026 (class period February 27, 2025 to July 8, 2026). Upcoming catalysts unchanged: 10-Q with MW-shipped/ASP detail (September 11), Q3 earnings (October). Motley Fool

FuelCell Energy (FCEL) and Ceres Power (CWR.L): No new corporate announcements today. FCEL's Torrington 500 MW/yr expansion and Ceres' Goldman Sachs Conviction Buy remain the live storylines heading into Q3 FY2026 (October) and H1 2026 (September) results respectively.

lcoe.text: Gas price case needs updating (see Top Signal #3): EIA's August STEO cut the 2026 Henry Hub forecast to $3.44/MMBtu (Q3 average $2.87/MMBtu). This is the second consecutive downward STEO revision (July STEO: $3.67/MMBtu) and now sits well below the model's legacy $4.00-4.90/MMBtu background assumption. Recommend retiring that legacy range in favor of the EIA STEO trajectory as the new base case, with $2.50-3.00/MMBtu as the near-term (2026) scenario. EIA STEO

PJM curtailment-risk pricing now has a concrete anchor (see Top Signal #1): Non-self-supplied large loads face curtailment compensated at only 50% of the existing demand-response penalty rate starting June 1, 2027. That discount is a usable proxy for the "cost of not self-supplying" in PJM territory, i.e. the value SOFC captures by removing that curtailment exposure entirely, once PJM publishes the specific dollar penalty rate after the October 12, 2026 effective date. Extract the rate when published and pair it with the expedited BYONG interconnection-track timeline as a second, faster-deployment value driver.
